title: Structured Output — JSON Schema, Pydantic, Zod, Constrained Decoding

questions.question: Which fields are required by INVOICE_SCHEMA at the root?
options: customer, line_items, total_usd, and currency
customer and discount only
sku, qty, and unit_usd
currency plus a free-form metadata object is required
questions.explanation: The root required list contains customer, line_items, total_usd, and currency; discount and metadata are not part of the schema.

questions.question: How does process_model_output classify text beginning with __REFUSAL__?
options: As valid invoice JSON after stripping the prefix
A refusal with its stripped reason
As a schema violation caused by an unknown field
As a parse_error because refusal text is not JSON
questions.explanation: The refusal marker is handled before JSON parsing, producing kind refusal and preserving the text after the marker as the reason.

questions.question: What kind does the trailing-comma invoice fixture produce?
options: ok, because JSON parsers ignore trailing commas
violation, because total_usd is not numeric
parse_error
refusal, because the model declined the invoice
questions.explanation: The fixture is syntactically invalid JSON, so decoding fails before schema validation can run.

questions.question: Why does the bad line-item fixture fail validation?
options: USD is not one of the allowed currencies
The customer string is too long
line_items must be a scalar number
bad SKU plus an extra discount field
questions.explanation: SKUs must match uppercase letters, digits, and hyphens, and line items disallow the undeclared discount property.

questions.question: What result kind and total should the happy Acme fixture produce?
options: kind ok with total_usd 219.98 and currency USD
kind refusal with total 0
kind parse_error because line_items is an array
kind violation because customer is a string
questions.explanation: The happy fixture satisfies the schema and reports the stated 219.98 USD invoice, so processing returns kind ok.

questions.question: What does strict provider mode change in this lesson?
options: It converts typed refusals into successful invoices
Strict blocks parse/schema errors, not refusals
It removes the currency enum and accepts arbitrary keys
It validates only the customer field
questions.explanation: Constrained decoding prevents malformed or schema-invalid model output, but the provider can still explicitly refuse the request.
